026 · Render-quality gap audit (Phase 1)

Vela, 2026-10-19. Audit only: no kit, generator, world or Unity change. Evidence sources: contracts/world/kit.json, out/world/harbour-district.world.json (rebuilt export on disk), unity/Assets/Suborned/Editor/World/*, unity/Assets/Suborned/Shaders/*, the old project ~/Projects/the-suborned/game/Assets/TheSuborned/Art/DecoKit, the store ~/Projects/the-suborned-store/source-art/DecoKit, perf record out/perf/b6-2026-10-14-fbf540e.json (Air, Mac16,13). Numbers marked est. are my estimates, not measurements. Latch's baseline set (briefs/026/baseline/) did not exist when I finished; the current-state pictures below are the latest existing in-game captures (briefs/020, briefs/008) and must be replaced by the baseline stops when it lands.

0 · The short version

The kit is not the problem; the ground, the street life and the surfaces are. The current kit.json (301 pieces: 174 adopted) is a superset of the old DecoKit (202). 100 percent of the 972 facade bays, 947 trees, all crossing parts and 98 percent of street furniture already come from the kit. What the old DecoKit city had and the new world does not: a populated street (robots with live faces, vending machines, parked and moving cars, tram, sky traffic: section 4b), textured, normal-mapped ground (asphalt, granite kerb, gutter setts, paving flags, lawn: 12 materials never reach Unity), rooftop gardens and roof pieces (111 roofs still draw spheres and boxes where the paintings show planted terraces), and signage with artwork (910 of 1,077 frontages are procedural stand-ins with flat sign boxes). On top of that the frame is over-bright, so none of the little form that exists shows.

Top 6 gaps, in order (re-ranked after the original-art review)

  1. Ground is flat colour. Roads, kerbs, pavement, quay, park, median: Layers.Ground makes ribbons and prisms in plain URP/Lit, smoothness 0.1, value 1, no texture, no normal, no gutter, no setts. The old kit shipped asphalt_road/warm/fine, granite_kerb, gutter_setts, pave_flags, lawn with normals and masks, and the old world laid them as world-metre UV meshes. Only the civic square carries a paving texture.
  2. The street has no life in it (new). The old world placed nine kit robots with live dot-matrix faces and servo heads, vending machines in pairs, an Automat, a kerb programme every 10 m (bins, racks, phone booth, hydrant, lightbox, scooter), parked cars in most kerb gaps, moving traffic, a tram, sky-rail trains, four aircar lanes, rocket flights, and a 3,000-agent crowd. Today: robots only as procedural boxes (5 of the 8 robot meshes unplaced), the DK_RobotFace shader is in Unity but its driver and glyphs were never ported, 0 vending machines, no ambient vehicle or tram or sky traffic (the data exists in life.json and transit.skyRail, nothing draws it), and the DecoKit candidates (14 Furnish, 16 Alleys, 10 billboards, 9 Sky, 6 Vehicles) are unplaced.
  3. Light and material response read bright and flat (Glint's phase; materials are my half): stone, enamel and chrome sit within a narrow value band, matte smoothness everywhere, no ambient occlusion on ground, no contact darkening at the kerb, haze flat to the horizon.
  4. Roofs are partly primitives. Correction: the 19 Oct export already names kit pieces for 248 of 359 roofs (Roof_Tank 92, Roof_Mast 120, Conservatory 11, pools 12, tennis 1), so the yellow balls and orange blocks in the briefs/020 captures predate it. Still primitive: 111 roofs (39 roof-gardens, 20 sign frames, 9 barrel vaults, 7 saucers, 3 dishes ...) with 1,030 trim boxes and 424 “park” spheres; Roof_Cabana and Roof_Planter are adopted but unplaced; the old roof themes (lido, bandstand lawn, glasshouse, deck) are not used.
  5. Plants are thin. Five adopted plant meshes (CoconutPalm, FanPalm, Cypress and two Play LODs) plus three bed tufts; planters are bare green blobs with dots, not the painted flowering masses; park and lawn are flat green; the lawn texture and four shrub/topiary candidates sit unadopted.
  6. Frontages, signage and building depth. 910 of 1,077 frontages are source: procedural (box front, awning, sign; motif/icon only as a palette key); no marquee, no billboard, no sandwich board, no hanging basket or window box; awnings are swatch stripes; the 310 skinned masses have no cornice, reveal or corner pilaster.

1 · The bar

Skyline bar: briefs/007/concepts/AtomicAge and Blocks sheets; hero painting (briefs/008/concepts/...city-hero) for the whole city. Latch's baseline stops (play zoom 14 at 38 degrees, yaw 30 and 210, street level, skyline) will go here: briefs/026/baseline/ (absent at write time).

2 · What the old DecoKit had

  • Manifest: 202 assets in 20 categories (Facades 22, Furnish 21, Ground 27, Alleys 16, Signage 15, Rooftop 14, Skyline 11, Street 9, Sky 9, Plaza 8, Plants 7, Landmarks 7 ...), about 1.42 M triangles total. Materials: 113, of which 25 stone, 21 enamel, 22 emissive, 8 fabric, 8 ceramic, 6 alpha cutouts. 25 carry a texture; 13 a normal map; 7 a mask (AO/roughness packed). Textures: 45 PNGs (about 125 MB on disk; about 177 MB est. as BC7 with mips, dominated by pave_flags at 4096 × 3 maps = 67 MB est.). Shaders: DK_LitCutaway, DK_ComplexLitCutaway (cutaway fade), DK_Ocean, DK_ShadowCatcher, DK_SpaceSky, DK_Contrail, DK_RobotFace. Source art: 15 generated sources (Textures/gen, Runware via textures.json), derived normals and masks (Textures/derived, 40 files), 5 HDRIs (city, courtyard, studio, sunrise, sunset), 94 icons.
  • The old city was built by the old project's Editor/World from 164 Generated/*.asset meshes (CityMass tiles, Circus ring road, verge, island, apron, bay) wearing the textured DK materials above. I found no scene in the old project, so I cannot say it renders as-is; Latch to judge whether briefs/026/old-decokit/ is feasible. The icon sheets below are the only ready-made old-kit pictures.

4 · Gap per family

Buildings (facades, corners, roofs, trim, glazing, depth)

  • Had: 22 facade pieces, 14 rooftop pieces, 5 highrise, 7 landmarks, 7 crowns, textured limestone with normal and mask, hull panels, ashlar texture.
  • Now: facade bays good (kit); the 737 masses behind and between them are flat boxes with swatch skins, no podium cornice, no corner pilaster, no recessed reveal, no glass depth (glass is a dark swatch plus a diagonal sheen); 111 of 359 roofs still primitive; Records Office is a plain volume with a smooth stone shell, not the painting's fluted-pier, brass-framed entrance with steps and globe.
  • Gap: depth (reveal, cornice, string course, parapet) and roofs (terraces, domes, planters). Candidates to adopt: Tower_*, Roof_Conservatory/Planter/Bandstand/Cabana, HallBay.

Plants

  • Had: 7 plant meshes, 6 alpha-cutout leaf materials, lawn texture with normal, flower clusters in three corals.
  • Now: 947 tree instances from 3 species; beds are bump tufts; lawn flat.
  • Gap: massed flowering planters on parapets and terraces (the paintings' defining plant read), variety (a second palm, olive or ficus, vines, hanging baskets), lawn and meadow material, tree pits.

Signage

  • Had: 15 signage pieces (blade signs, marquee, billboards in 3 forms, sandwich board), art textures (billboard_ads, poster_travel, banner_comet seafoam/teal, decals_transit sheet of 16 plates), neon (emissive) materials.
  • Now: 5 adopted; 10 candidates (Billboard_*, Marquee_Cinema, SandwichBoard); sign faces are boxes; no lettering anywhere in the world.
  • Gap: authored faces per trade (35 trades in the export), awning fabric, lettering/pictogram vocabulary (restraint: no readable text in play per brief 014, so pictogram and motif plates), wayfinding.

Roads, kerbs, gutters, setts, paving bands

  • Had: 27 ground pieces, asphalt_road (2048), asphalt_fine, asphalt_warm, granite_kerb, gutter_setts, pave_flags, lawn, terrazzo with normals and masks; ManholeCover, DrainGrate, tram rail tile.
  • Now: ribbons in flat colour; 13 adopted Ground pieces are crossing parts and inlay bands only.
  • Gap: everything on the list above except the inlays.

Pedestrian crossings (brief 009)

  • Geometry and glow match the concept: 116 sites, floating SignalEye orbs (207), flush dot rows and fields, studs (704). Gaps: brass hairline frame along the strip (open since brief 009), a texture under it (the concept's asphalt is a dark, slightly violet fine-grain surface with warm sun patches), kerb return and flush ramp detail, contact AO.

Street furniture

  • Mostly there (24 of 32 kinds, 98 percent of items, are kit). Gap: the procedural kinds (lamps 108, timetable columns, vending robots, station entrances, kiosks, police posts, robot docks); small items from the old kit (manhole, drain, utility cabinet, sandwich board, bike rack) for street-level life; every enamel piece is matte and the same palette; brass is a hairline rule that few pieces yet carry.

4b · Original art not in the world: what the old world had in it

Correction taken (Sky): the old art was not concept only. The old Unity project was a built, populated world. Source read: ~/Projects/the-suborned/game/Assets/TheSuborned/Editor/DecoKit/*.cs (60 builders: CityPlan, CityBlocks, CityMass, StreetLayout, StreetLife, DistrictDressing, DistrictLife, Southside, SouthsideLife, Decks, Roofline, RoofThemes, Gardens, Harbour, Circus, SkyRail, SkyTraffic, Robots, Citizens, CrowdMerge, RoadMarkings ...), Scripts/Robots (RobotFace, RobotIdle), Scripts/Sky (SkyPath, SkyTraffic, RocketFlight), Scripts/Crowd (VatCrowd and friends), Scripts/Civic, Art/RetroFutureMobility, Art/Citizens3D/crowd, and the store (~/Projects/the-suborned-store). Latch's scratch rebuild of the old world (briefs/026/old-decokit/) had no shots yet when I finished; drop them here when they land. Every placement figure below is read from builder code, not counted from a run.

Siting note. The old layout is hand-authored: explicit coordinates per robot, vending machine and terrace. The rule in force now (nothing hand-placed; street furniture goes where a real city puts it; coverage gaps go to Sky, never forced) means each of these becomes a generator rule over plan data (frontage trade, stop, kerb bay, station), not a port of coordinates. The old rules above are the starting vocabulary for those rules.

The concept source for anything we still have no model for

Store concepts/Props (22 sheets, six designs each; Seedream 5.0 Pro; 26 Sep to 2 Oct), Robots/lean (4 comic-style robot sheets with glass display faces: robots, service, corp, makers), Streets, Nature, District, Horizon. The 22 sheets: advert columns, aircar kerbside (fuel pumps and chargers), benches, bollards, food carts, fountains, market stalls, news kiosks, personal mobility, planters, post and parcel, robots civic, robots service, security points, street lamps, traffic signals, tram shelters, transit kiosks, utility, videophone booths, wayfinding. Many are the source of kit pieces already built (Streetlamp, Bench, Bollard, Hydrant, BusShelter, PhoneBooth, PneumaticPost, AdColumn); the rest are not modelled: aircar chargers and fuel pumps, food carts (six: rocket, popcorn dome, gelato), market stalls (six), personal mobility (bubble car, wheel, jet-pack scooter), parcel robots and lockers, security points (call posts, sirens, camera eyes), wayfinding signposts and compass inlay, transit kiosks (globe, jukebox-style), benches (the pod and clamshell types), fountains (atom, tiered, wall), robots_civic (street sweeper, mech, wheel monopod, biped hopper, gardener, saucer).

What would need Sky's pick before anything is modelled from these: which of the six designs per sheet (the sheets show six each), and whether the glass-face comic robots or the DecoKit dot-matrix robots are the city's robots. Concept art first stands: nothing new to be modelled until Sky picks from these existing sheets (no new Runware spend needed for them).

5 · Cost frame (Air, 60 fps)

The only measured Air record is 2026-10-14 (b6-2026-10-14-fbf540e.json, world only, before brief 009 crossings, brief 020 stand-in visuals, people and vehicles; export 9b2b451d): frame p50 / p95 ms: home 5.6 / 8.5 (161 fps), cafe-square 6.0 / 9.0, parade 6.7 / 10.7, crown-circus 5.0 / 7.6, harbour-quay 4.2 / 6.3, heaviest 12.8 / 27.3 (74 fps); home: 1.47 M triangles, 88 SetPass calls. Open facts from Redline and the handoff: the architecture fade (discard) roughly halves the heaviest frame; SSAO costs 24 to 35 percent; Redline's proposed world budget is ≤ 9 ms GPU. The record's gpuMs p50 (home 10.2) is above its frame time, so I use frame ms. Current headroom is unknown: the world has grown since, and the harness must be re-run before and after each round.

Texture-memory estimates use BC7 (1 byte per pixel, × 1.33 for mips); Unity project import settings decide the real figure.

Order logic. 1 first (free, and every later before/after reads against it); 2 next (the ground fills most of the frame); 3 and 4 right behind it because they are the cheapest visible change (robots and vending machines are already modelled and adopted or one adopt away, and the old world proves they work), and because Sky has already called them out; then crossings, buildings and roofs (5 to 7); then vehicles, plants and sky traffic (8 to 10), which need Sky picks or concept sheets; signage and fillers last. Each round: shot on the baseline stops, then measured on the Air with the same perf plan (briefs/008/perf/scripts/run.sh) before the next begins; stop adding if the heaviest stop passes 13 ms p50 (12.8 ms at the last measurement) or the world exceeds the 9 ms GPU proposal.
